question: From the incisal aspect of the permanent mandibular canine, the cingulum is: (Tests)
explanation: Correct answer: A. Offset slightly toward the distal

question: The normal chronological eruption time for the permanent mandibular canine is: (Tests)
explanation: Correct answer: B. 9 to 10 years

question: On proximal views of the permanent mandibular canine, the labial surface curvature from the cusp tip to the cervical line exhibits: (Tests)
options: A continuous, smooth convex arc from the cervical line to the cusp tip
A distinct angular plateau in the middle third
A sharp concavity in the incisal third
A perfectly straight vertical vertical plane
explanation: Correct answer: A. A continuous, smooth convex arc from the cervical line to the cusp tip

question: The developmental depressions on the mesial and distal root surfaces of the permanent mandibular canine are: (Tests)
options: Deep longitudinal grooves, with the developmental depression on the distal being deeper
Confined exclusively to the apical 1 mm
explanation: Correct answer: B. Deep longitudinal grooves, with the developmental depression on the distal being deeper

question: The Universal Number for the permanent mandibular left canine is: (Tests)
explanation: Correct answer: B. 22

question: The Universal Number for the permanent mandibular right canine is: (Tests)
explanation: Correct answer: C. 27

question: From the labial aspect, the permanent mandibular canine cusp tip: (Tests)
options: Is blunt and situated directly over the center or slightly mesial of the root bisector
Extends far distally beyond the distal root outline
Is sharp and needle-like like a primary canine
Is level with the distal contact area
Tilted 45 degrees toward the labial line angle
explanation: Correct answer: A. Is blunt and situated directly over the center or slightly mesial of the root bisector

question: Which of the following anterior teeth typically exhibits the greatest bilateral symmetry of its crown from the labial aspect?
explanation: Correct answer: B. Permanent mandibular central incisor

question: The first succedaneous tooth to erupt into the human oral cavity is the: (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: A. Mandibular central incisors

question: Which of the following is the smallest tooth in the human permanent dentition? (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: B. Permanent mandibular central incisor

question: The incisal ridge of the permanent mandibular central incisor, when viewed from the mesial or distal aspect, is characteristically positioned:
options: Directly centered over the root bisector
Lingual to the long-axis bisecting line of the root
Labial to the long-axis bisecting line of the root
Slanted 45 degrees toward the labial border
Curved entirely toward the facial embrasure
explanation: Correct answer: B. Lingual to the long-axis bisecting line of the root

question: The permanent mandibular lateral incisor can be readily differentiated from the permanent mandibular central incisor because the incisal edge of the lateral incisor: (Past Paper)
options: Is completely straight and parallel to the labial axis
Is twisted distolingually on the root base to follow the curvature of the dental arch
Has a mesioincisal angle that is more rounded than its distoincisal angle
Is located distinctly labial to the root bisector
explanation: Correct answer: B. Is twisted distolingually on the root base to follow the curvature of the dental arch

question: In the permanent mandibular central incisor, the mesioincisal and distoincisal angles from the labial aspect are characteristically:
options: Both sharp, nearly right angles (with the mesioincisal slightly sharper)
Both broadly rounded with an obtuse outline
Well rounded distally with an incisal slope
Asymmetrical with an elevated distal margin
explanation: Correct answer: A. Both sharp, nearly right angles (with the mesioincisal slightly sharper)

question: From the incisal aspect, the incisal ridge of the permanent mandibular central incisor is oriented:
options: At an exact 90-degree right angle to the labiolingual bisecting line
Twisted noticeably toward the distolingual aspect
Slanted markedly toward the facial line angle
Curved into a broad convex U-shape
explanation: Correct answer: A. At an exact 90-degree right angle to the labiolingual bisecting line

question: On the mesial and distal root surfaces of the permanent mandibular central incisor, the longitudinal developmental depressions:
options: Are completely absent, leaving smooth convex surfaces
Result in a root that is wider mesiodistally than labiolingually
Are shallow depressions that frequently terminate in bifurcation
Present as distinct, broad concavities running most of the root length
Are located solely in the coronal third of the root
explanation: Correct answer: D. Present as distinct, broad concavities running most of the root length

question: The permanent mandibular lateral incisor crown compared with that of the permanent mandibular central incisor is:
options: Exactly identical in all millimeter dimensions
Slightly longer and narrower in all dimensions
Slightly wider mesiodistally and longer cervicoincisally
explanation: Correct answer: E. Slightly wider mesiodistally and longer cervicoincisally

question: In cross section at the cementoenamel junction, the root of the permanent mandibular central incisor is:
options: Triangular with the apex pointing lingually
Perfectly circular without any flat areas
Kidney-shaped with an exclusively mesial notch
explanation: Correct answer: E. Narrow mesiodistally and elongated labiolingually (ovoid/ribbon-like)

question: The lingual surface of the permanent mandibular central incisor compared to the permanent maxillary central incisor is:
options: Far deeper with prominent fossae and deep pits
Characterized by a massive, bifurcated cingulum
Noticeably smoother with very indistinct marginal ridges and a shallow lingual fossa
Interrupted by a distinct palatogingival groove
explanation: Correct answer: C. Noticeably smoother with very indistinct marginal ridges and a shallow lingual fossa

question: What is the usual chronological age range for the clinical eruption of the permanent mandibular central incisor?
explanation: Correct answer: B. 6 to 7 years

question: What is the chronological age range for the clinical eruption of the permanent mandibular lateral incisor?
explanation: Correct answer: B. 7 to 8 years

question: On the mesial aspect of the permanent mandibular central incisor, the cervical line (CEJ) curves incisally by approximately:
explanation: Correct answer: B. 3.0 mm

question: In the permanent mandibular lateral incisor, the distoincisal angle from the labial aspect:
options: Forms a sharp 90-degree right angle identical to the mesial angle
Is noticeably more rounded than its mesioincisal angle
Tapers directly to a sharp cuspal point
Slants sharply into the cervical third
Is located further incisally than the mesioincisal angle
explanation: Correct answer: B. Is noticeably more rounded than its mesioincisal angle

question: The mesial contact area of the permanent mandibular lateral incisor is located:
options: In the cervical third of the crown
In the incisal third, near the incisal edge
At the middle of the middle third
At the junction of the middle and cervical thirds
explanation: Correct answer: B. In the incisal third, near the incisal edge

question: The distal contact area of the permanent mandibular lateral incisor is positioned:
options: Slightly more cervically than the mesial contact (incisal third near the junction of the incisal and middle thirds)
Exactly at the same level as the mesioincisal line angle
explanation: Correct answer: B. Slightly more cervically than the mesial contact (incisal third near the junction of the incisal and middle thirds)

question: From the incisal aspect of the permanent mandibular lateral incisor, the lingual cingulum appears:
options: Perfectly centered on the mesiodistal axis
Continuous with a prominent labial ridge
explanation: Correct answer: B. Displaced slightly toward the distal

question: When viewing the mesial surface of the permanent mandibular lateral incisor, the labial crest of contour is located in the:
options: Junction of the middle and incisal thirds
Cervical third (just above the cervical line)
explanation: Correct answer: D. Cervical third (just above the cervical line)

question: A single root canal is most typical for mandibular incisors; however, when two canals occur due to a labiolingual division, they are termed:
explanation: Correct answer: C. Labial and lingual canals

question: The curvature of the root apex in the permanent mandibular lateral incisor is most frequently directed toward the:
explanation: Correct answer: A. Distal

question: How many developmental lobes contribute to the formation of the permanent mandibular central incisor crown?
options: Four lobes (three labial and one lingual forming the cingulum)
explanation: Correct answer: A. Four lobes (three labial and one lingual forming the cingulum)

question: The mamelons of permanent mandibular central incisors:
options: Persist throughout the patient's entire adult life
Are three rounded enamel prominences on newly erupted incisal ridges that wear down flat with normal masticatory attrition
Form the primary boundary of the lingual fossa
Develop strictly from the lingual cingulum lobe
explanation: Correct answer: B. Are three rounded enamel prominences on newly erupted incisal ridges that wear down flat with normal masticatory attrition

question: From the incisal aspect, the permanent mandibular central incisor crown displays a labial surface that is:
options: Sharply peaked into a prominent facial ridge
Noticeably concave across the incisal third
Convex cervically, but relatively flat in the incisal third mesiodistally
Extremely asymmetrical toward the distal side
Distinctly notched by the distolingual groove
explanation: Correct answer: C. Convex cervically, but relatively flat in the incisal third mesiodistally

question: Root completion for the permanent mandibular central incisor is typically achieved at:
explanation: Correct answer: D. 9 years of age

question: Between the two mandibular permanent incisors, the tooth that exhibits the greater cervicoincisal crown length is the:
options: Both are strictly identical in crown height
Mandibular central incisor by more than 2 mm
explanation: Correct answer: A. Mandibular lateral incisor

question: The lingual fossa of the permanent mandibular lateral incisor is:
options: Divided by an exaggerated transverse enamel ridge
Marked by a deep, highly carious lingual pit
Completely absent, showing a uniform lingual convexity
A smooth, shallow concavity bordered by subtle marginal ridges
Occupied by an accessory lingual cusp
explanation: Correct answer: D. A smooth, shallow concavity bordered by subtle marginal ridges

question: From the proximal aspects, the incisal ridge of both permanent mandibular central and lateral incisors is positioned:
options: Labial to the root vertical axis
Parallel to the distal contact point
Lingual to (or on) the vertical long axis of the tooth
2 mm labial to the cervical line
explanation: Correct answer: C. Lingual to (or on) the vertical long axis of the tooth

question: In newly erupted maxillary incisor, complete incisal portion is made up of incisal ridge that is rounded and merges with mesio-incisal and disto-incisal angles. Occlusal wear incisal edge is formed by the junction of: (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: B. Labial and lingual surfaces

question: The geometric outlines of labial and lingual surfaces of maxillary central incisor are trapezoid in shape with longest uneven side on incisal edge. In this way, mesio-distal diameter of the crown is lesser at cervical line than incisal edge; (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: D. more than 2 mm

question: Developmental defects on the enamel surface of maxillary lateral incisor are most common. They can be genetically induced or acquired due to metabolic disturbances, infections, or drugs and their location is associated with timing of events in relation to chronology of tooth development. First evidence of calcification of maxillary lateral incisor appears post-natal at: (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: D. 1 to 2 years after birth

question: Maxillary lateral incisor supplements maxillary central incisor in functions, However maxillary lateral incisors can be differentiated predominantly from maxillary central incisors in resemblance in following ways. The first evidence of calcification of maxillary central incisor appears post-natal at: (Past Paper)
options: All maxillary lateral incisors exhibit more convexity labially and lingually from the incisal aspect
The cervical-incisal length of crown on the average measures 1mm smaller than that of the central incisor
The mesial outline of the crown has more rounded mesio-incisal angle than that of the central incisor
The distal outline is always more rounded than that of the central incisor
The crown and root of maxillary lateral incisor is smaller in all dimensions
explanation: Correct answer: B. The cervical-incisal length of crown on the average measures 1mm smaller than that of the central incisor

question: Which of the following dental condition is found in patients with down's syndrome: (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: B. Shovel shaped incisors

question: Presence of exaggerated marginal ridges on the lingual surface of incisors, most commonly observed in Mongoloids, is known as:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Shovel-shaped incisors

question: The most variable anterior teeth in permanent dentition, which sometimes possess a tubercle on the cingulum, peg-shaped crown, or presence of a palatogingival (palatoradicular) groove, is the:
explanation: Correct answer: A. Maxillary lateral incisor

question: In young individuals the shape of the pulp chamber of permanent maxillary central incisor is:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Triangular

question: Which of the following anterior teeth have the largest dimension of pulp chamber? (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: A. Maxillary Central incisors

question: From the labial aspect of the permanent maxillary central incisor, the mesioincisal angle is:
options: Broadly rounded with a wide radius
Sharp and nearly a right angle (90 degrees)
explanation: Correct answer: D. Sharp and nearly a right angle (90 degrees)

question: On the lingual surface of the permanent maxillary central incisor, the broad, smooth concavity bounded by the marginal ridges, cingulum, and incisal ridge is the:
explanation: Correct answer: D. Lingual fossa

question: From the mesial aspect of the permanent maxillary central incisor, the incisal ridge of the crown is positioned:
options: Significantly lingual to the long-axis bisecting line
Significantly labial to the long-axis bisecting line
Centered directly on a line bisecting the center of the root
explanation: Correct answer: D. Centered directly on a line bisecting the center of the root

question: The cervical line (cementoenamel junction) of the permanent maxillary central incisor exhibits its greatest curvature towards the incisal on which surface?
options: It exhibits equal curvature on all four surfaces
explanation: Correct answer: A. Mesial surface (approximately 3.5 mm curvature)

question: In cross-section at the cervical line, the root of the permanent maxillary central incisor is generally:
options: Triangular with a rounded base on the labial and apex on the lingual
Severely compressed mesiodistally into a ribbon shape
Kidney-shaped with a deep mesial concavity
Perfectly circular without any flat areas
explanation: Correct answer: A. Triangular with a rounded base on the labial and apex on the lingual

question: Compared with the maxillary central incisor, the permanent maxillary lateral incisor typically has a crown that is:
explanation: Correct answer: A. Shorter cervicoincisally and narrower mesiodistally

question: The distoincisal angle of the permanent maxillary lateral incisor from the labial aspect is characterized by being:
options: Well rounded with the crest of contour placed more cervically
Completely absent due to incisal wear
Sharper than the mesioincisal angle of the central incisor
explanation: Correct answer: B. Well rounded with the crest of contour placed more cervically

question: A distinct developmental groove that frequently originates in the lingual pit of the maxillary lateral incisor and extends onto the cingulum and root trunk, predisposing to localized periodontal breakdown, is the:
explanation: Correct answer: D. Palatogingival (palatoradicular) groove

question: The permanent maxillary lateral incisor root in its apical third characteristically curves toward the:
explanation: Correct answer: C. Distal

question: A severe developmental anomaly of the permanent maxillary lateral incisor where the crown fails to develop its normal mesiodistal dimensions and tapers to a sharp, conical point is known as a:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Peg lateral

question: An invagination of the enamel organ into the dental papilla that occurs most frequently in permanent maxillary lateral incisors, giving the radiographic appearance of a "tooth within a tooth", is:
explanation: Correct answer: D. Dens invaginatus (dens in dente)

question: From the incisal aspect, the incisal ridge of the permanent maxillary central incisor runs:
options: Straight mesiodistally, bisecting the crown labiolingually
In a sharp crescent with the concavity facing labially
At a 45-degree angle to the dental arch
Lingually into the center of the cingulum
explanation: Correct answer: B. Straight mesiodistally, bisecting the crown labiolingually

question: In the permanent maxillary central incisor, the mesial contact area is positioned:
options: At the junction of the incisal and middle thirds
In the middle of the middle third
In the incisal third, very close to the mesioincisal angle
Exactly at the center of the labial surface
explanation: Correct answer: D. In the incisal third, very close to the mesioincisal angle

question: The lingual surface of the permanent maxillary lateral incisor compared with that of the maxillary central incisor displays:
options: More pronounced marginal ridges and a deeper, more circumscribed lingual fossa/pit
A completely flat contour with no cingulum
explanation: Correct answer: C. More pronounced marginal ridges and a deeper, more circumscribed lingual fossa/pit

question: On the labial surface of newly erupted permanent maxillary central incisors, the two shallow vertical depressions that divide the surface into three labial lobes are termed:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Mesial and distal developmental depressions

question: What is the chronological age range for the normal clinical eruption of the permanent maxillary central incisor?
explanation: Correct answer: A. 7 to 8 years

question: What is the chronological age range for the normal clinical eruption of the permanent maxillary lateral incisor?
explanation: Correct answer: C. 8 to 9 years

question: The oblique ridge is formed by the union of:
options: Triangular ridge of the distobuccal cusp and distal cusp ridge of the mesiolingual cusp
Triangular ridge of the mesiobuccal cusp and triangular ridge of the mesiolingual cusp
Triangular ridge of the distobuccal cusp and mesial cusp ridge of the distolingual cusp
Mesial marginal ridge and distal marginal ridge
Triangular ridge of the distobuccal cusp and triangular ridge of the distolingual cusp
explanation: Correct answer: A. Triangular ridge of the distobuccal cusp and distal cusp ridge of the mesiolingual cusp

question: The tooth having both trigon and talon is:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Maxillary molar

question: Distal side of the trigon on permanent maxillary molars is formed by:
explanation: Correct answer: A. Oblique ridge

question: Which of the following is the largest cusp of the permanent maxillary 1st molar?
explanation: Correct answer: C. Mesiolingual cusp
yearSource: Oral Biology Proff 2025 / Mock OB Batch 10

question: Which cusp decreases most markedly in size across the permanent maxillary molar series from first to third molar?
explanation: Correct answer: D. Distolingual cusp

question: When we talk about the permanent maxillary second molar, which of the following is the most poorly developed cusp? (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: D. Distolingual

question: Shape of the permanent maxillary second molar from the occlusal aspect when the distolingual cusp is absent/rudimentary is: (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: B. Heart-shaped

question: Which root of the permanent maxillary 1st molar is the longest? (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: C. Palatal/lingual root

question: The fourth root canal (MB2) if present in a maxillary first molar is usually located in the:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Mesiobuccal root

question: In permanent molars, the supplementary cusp of Carabelli is present in around what percentage of teeth?
explanation: Correct answer: B. 60%

question: The largest permanent tooth in the mandibular arch is: (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: A. Mandibular first molar

question: What is the occlusal geometric shape of the permanent mandibular first molar?
explanation: Correct answer: C. Pentagonal (or Hexagonal/Trapezoidal)

question: What is the occlusal geometric shape of the permanent mandibular second molar?
options: Rectangular (four equal cusps divided by a cross "+" groove)
explanation: Correct answer: D. Rectangular (four equal cusps divided by a cross "+" groove)

question: Which of the following is true regarding the pulp cavities of the permanent mandibular first molar? (Past Paper)
options: It typically has two roots and three root canals
Frequently it has a fourth canal in a separate root
It typically has three roots and three root canals
It typically has four apical foramina
explanation: Correct answer: A. It typically has two roots and three root canals

question: The dimension of permanent mandibular molars mesiodistally versus buccolingually:
options: Highly variable with no consistent pattern
explanation: Correct answer: A. Mesiodistally larger than buccolingually

question: Which cusp of the permanent mandibular first molar is the largest?
explanation: Correct answer: B. Mesiobuccal cusp

question: The mesiolingual cusp of a permanent maxillary molar occludes with what on the mandibular molar?
options: Central fossa of the mandibular molar
explanation: Correct answer: B. Central fossa of the mandibular molar

question: An endodontist negotiating the mesiobuccal root of a permanent maxillary first molar in a 24-year-old patient detects a distinct second canal orifice (MB2). According to Wheeler's, where is this orifice positioned relative to the main mesiobuccal (MB1) canal?
options: 2 to 3 mm lingual/palatal and slightly mesial to the MB1 orifice
Directly within the palatal canal floor
Exactly halfway across the oblique ridge
explanation: Correct answer: B. 2 to 3 mm lingual/palatal and slightly mesial to the MB1 orifice

question: During access cavity preparation on a permanent maxillary first molar, the clinician notes the rhomboidal outline of the pulp chamber floor. The canal orifice located most distally and closest to the center of the tooth is the:
explanation: Correct answer: A. Distobuccal canal

question: A periodontist evaluates a deep 8 mm pocket on the mesial surface of a permanent maxillary first molar. Radiographs show horizontal bone loss reaching the root trunk. Why is root instrumentation and plaque removal particularly challenging on the mesial surface of this maxillary molar compared to its distal surface?
options: The mesial furcation is located significantly further apically than the distal furcation
The mesial furcation opens much closer to the palatal surface than the buccal surface, beneath a broad mesial crown concavity
The distobuccal root completely overlaps the mesial surface
The mesial surface has a prominent tubercle of Zuckerkandl
An enamel pearl is present in 100% of mesial furcations
explanation: Correct answer: B. The mesial furcation opens much closer to the palatal surface than the buccal surface, beneath a broad mesial crown concavity

question: In a restorative procedure on a permanent mandibular first molar, a clinician prepares an occlusal cavity. When restoring the marginal ridges, they must remember that unlike the mesial marginal ridge, the distal marginal ridge is unique because:
options: It is significantly taller and sharper than the mesial marginal ridge
It is located more cervically, is shorter buccolingually, and is notched by a distal marginal groove
It is strictly horizontal without any developmental groove
It connects directly with the transverse ridge of the mesiolingual cusp
It bears a functional centric stop for the maxillary canine
explanation: Correct answer: B. It is located more cervically, is shorter buccolingually, and is notched by a distal marginal groove

question: A patient presents with acute pulpitis on tooth #30 (mandibular right first molar). After entering the distal canal, the dentist suspects a second distal canal (distolingual). What external anatomical variation in root morphology strongly correlates with the presence of two separate distal roots (radix entomolaris)?
options: A separate, supernumerary distolingual root emerging from the lingual root trunk
An accessory root arising exclusively from the facial bifurcation
A fusion between the mesial and distal root apices
A C-shaped root configuration connecting the buccal walls
explanation: Correct answer: A. A separate, supernumerary distolingual root emerging from the lingual root trunk

question: During a complicated extraction of a permanent mandibular second molar, an oral surgeon discovers that the mesial and distal roots are joined along the buccal aspect by a continuous web of radicular dentin and cementum, presenting a 180-degree ribbon-like canal configuration. This clinical exception is classified as:
explanation: Correct answer: B. C-shaped canal anatomy

question: A clinician carving a Class II amalgam restoration on a permanent maxillary first molar must reproduce the oblique ridge. If the bur erroneously cuts across this ridge from the central pit to the distal fossa, what anatomical feature of the natural tooth is being violated?
options: The oblique ridge is an uninterrupted enamel bridge elevated above the surrounding fossae that strengthens the crown against occlusal shear
The oblique ridge must always contain a deep developmental fissure separating the trigon and talon
The oblique ridge terminates entirely on the distolingual cusp
The oblique ridge runs parallel to the buccolingual axis
The oblique ridge is identical to the transverse ridge of a premolar
explanation: Correct answer: A. The oblique ridge is an uninterrupted enamel bridge elevated above the surrounding fossae that strengthens the crown against occlusal shear

question: A 19-year-old patient presents for orthodontic evaluation. The practitioner notes that tooth #18 (mandibular left second molar) displays an occlusal surface with four nearly equal quadrants separated by a straight central and lingual-buccal groove system. What occlusal groove pattern is this, and where does the central pit lie?
options: "Y" pattern with the pit offset to the distal
"+" (cross) pattern with the central pit located at the exact geometric center of the occlusal table
"H" pattern with the pit shifted mesially
Zigzag pattern passing around an oblique ridge
explanation: Correct answer: B. "+" (cross) pattern with the central pit located at the exact geometric center of the occlusal table

question: During periodontal scaling on the lingual aspect of a permanent maxillary first molar, the curette falls into a deep groove that extends from the occlusal surface, crosses between the mesiolingual and distolingual cusps, and fades onto the lingual surface of the palatal root. This structure is the:
options: Palatogingival groove of the lateral incisor
explanation: Correct answer: A. Lingual developmental groove (distolingual groove)

question: A patient sustains a fracture of the distobuccal cusp of a permanent mandibular first molar during heavy mastication. According to the morphology of mandibular molars, which developmental groove directly separates this fractured cusp from the smaller distal cusp?
explanation: Correct answer: B. Distobuccal developmental groove

question: In permanent maxillary molars, the talon is the distal component of the crown that was added phylogenetically. Which cusp constitutes the true talon?
explanation: Correct answer: D. Distolingual cusp

question: The trigon of a permanent maxillary molar consists of which triad of primary developmental cusps?
options: Mesiolingual, Distolingual, and Cusp of Carabelli
Mesiobuccal, Distolingual, and Cusp of Carabelli
explanation: Correct answer: A. Mesiobuccal, Mesiolingual, and Distobuccal cusps

question: When viewing the permanent mandibular first molar from the buccal aspect, the cervical line (CEJ) typically exhibits:
options: A sharp 3 mm curvature toward the occlusal surface
A straight line with no deviation
A small, sharp apical projection of enamel extending toward the bifurcation
A deep horizontal step onto the distal root
Complete absence of any line demarcation
explanation: Correct answer: C. A small, sharp apical projection of enamel extending toward the bifurcation

question: On the buccal surface of the permanent mandibular first molar, the mesiobuccal developmental groove frequently terminates in the middle third in a:
options: Distinct buccal pit (a common site for carious lesions)
explanation: Correct answer: B. Distinct buccal pit (a common site for carious lesions)

question: From the mesial aspect of a permanent mandibular first molar, the buccal crest of contour is located:
options: At the junction of the occlusal and middle thirds
In the middle third of the crown
In the cervical third, displaying a prominent buccal cervical ridge
At the level of the occlusal table
explanation: Correct answer: C. In the cervical third, displaying a prominent buccal cervical ridge

question: On the mesial aspect of a permanent mandibular first molar, the lingual crest of contour is located:
options: In the middle third of the crown
explanation: Correct answer: B. In the middle third of the crown

question: In cross-section at the mid-root level, the mesial root of a permanent mandibular first molar is characterized by:
options: An hourglass or kidney-shaped outline with deep concavities on both its mesial and distal surfaces
A triangular shape with apex to the lingual
A completely solid rod without internal pulp spaces
A square outline with sharp line angles
explanation: Correct answer: B. An hourglass or kidney-shaped outline with deep concavities on both its mesial and distal surfaces

question: The root trunk of the permanent mandibular first molar from the buccal aspect measures approximately what height from the cervical line to the bifurcation?
explanation: Correct answer: B. 3 mm

question: Compared with the permanent mandibular first molar, the root trunk of the permanent mandibular second molar is:
options: Longer, with roots that are less divergent and closer together
explanation: Correct answer: C. Longer, with roots that are less divergent and closer together

question: In the permanent maxillary first molar, which root typically exhibits both a buccal and a lingual longitudinal concavity along its root trunk and body?
explanation: Correct answer: C. Mesiobuccal root

question: From the occlusal aspect, the crown of the permanent maxillary first molar exhibits two acute line angles and two obtuse line angles. The two acute line angles are:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Mesiobuccal and distolingual

question: The two obtuse line angles on the occlusal table of the permanent maxillary first molar are:
explanation: Correct answer: C. Mesiolingual and distobuccal

question: On the occlusal surface of a permanent maxillary first molar, the cusp that gives rise to two distinct triangular ridges (one contributing to the transverse ridge and one to the oblique ridge) is the:
explanation: Correct answer: C. Mesiolingual cusp

question: The occlusal table of the permanent maxillary first molar contains two major fossae and two minor fossae. The two major fossae are:
options: Mesial triangular fossa and distal triangular fossa
explanation: Correct answer: A. Central fossa and distal fossa

question: What is the normal chronological age range for the clinical eruption of the permanent maxillary and mandibular first molars?
explanation: Correct answer: B. 6 to 7 years

question: What is the normal chronological age range for the clinical eruption of the permanent second molars?
explanation: Correct answer: D. 12 to 13 years

question: Root completion for the permanent first molars is typically achieved at:
explanation: Correct answer: C. 9 to 10 years

question: From the proximal view of a permanent maxillary molar, the palatal root exhibits a characteristic curvature that is often described as:
options: A straight peg with no deviation
A "banana-like" or flared outward curvature extending lingually past the crown outline, then curving buccally at the apex
Fused to the distobuccal root along its entire length
explanation: Correct answer: B. A "banana-like" or flared outward curvature extending lingually past the crown outline, then curving buccally at the apex

question: In the permanent mandibular first molar, the five cusps in decreasing order of size are:
explanation: Correct answer: A. MB > ML > DL > DB > Distal

question: The smallest and most variable functional cusp among the primary four cusps of the permanent maxillary second molar is the:
explanation: Correct answer: D. Distolingual cusp

question: The permanent maxillary third molar most commonly exhibits an occlusal outline that mimics which tooth?
options: Heart-shaped permanent maxillary second molar (with absent distolingual cusp)
explanation: Correct answer: B. Heart-shaped permanent maxillary second molar (with absent distolingual cusp)

question: Permanent mandibular third molars frequently show an irregular occlusal table characterized by:
options: An exaggerated "Y" pattern with no supplementary lines
A crenulated or "wrinkled" appearance with numerous supplemental grooves and fissures
A single transverse ridge connecting two cusps only
explanation: Correct answer: C. A crenulated or "wrinkled" appearance with numerous supplemental grooves and fissures

question: A peg-shaped molar or severe microdontia occurring in the permanent molar series is most frequently observed in:
explanation: Correct answer: D. Maxillary third molar

question: Cervical cross section of maxillary first premolar has:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Kidney shape

question: Which of the following statements are incorrect regarding max. 2nd premolar? (Past Paper)

Mesial marginal developmental groove is present across the marginal ridge
Crown is more rounded than maxillary first premolar
It typically possesses a single root
Occlusal table shows more supplemental grooves

question: The most common position for the mental foramen is?

Vertical line passing through the Mylohyoid ridge
Vertical line passing through the mandibular 2nd premolar
Vertical line passing through the mandibular 1st premolar
Vertical line passing through the mandibular canine

question: On the occlusal aspect of the permanent maxillary first premolar, the mesial marginal developmental groove characteristically crosses the mesial marginal ridge and terminates:
options: Directly in the mesial triangular fossa
Onto the mesial surface of the crown
Continuing onto the mesial developmental depression of the crown and root
Within the central pit without crossing the ridge
explanation: Correct answer: C. Continuing onto the mesial developmental depression of the crown and root

question: The mesial cusp ridge of the buccal cusp of the permanent maxillary first premolar is unique among premolars because it is:

Longer than the distal cusp ridge
explanation: Correct answer: D. Longer than the distal cusp ridge

question: The permanent maxillary first premolar typically possesses how many roots and pulp canals?
options: One single root and one canal
Two roots (buccal and palatal) and two root canals in the majority of cases
Three distinct roots and four canals
One fused root with three canals
Two roots with one single canal
explanation: Correct answer: B. Two roots (buccal and palatal) and two root canals in the majority of cases

question: In cross-section through the cervical line and root trunk, the permanent maxillary first premolar demonstrates a distinct outline that is:
options: Kidney-shaped (reniform) with a deep mesial concavity
Kidney-shaped (reniform) with a deep mesial concavity
explanation: Correct answer: E. Kidney-shaped (reniform) with a deep mesial concavity

question: The permanent maxillary second premolar differs from the permanent maxillary first premolar by possessing:
options: A single root and cusps of almost equal height, lacking a mesial marginal groove
A much sharper and longer buccal cusp
A deeper mesial radicular developmental depression
Two widely bifurcated roots in 85% of cases
A mesial cusp slope longer than its distal cusp slope
explanation: Correct answer: A. A single root and cusps of almost equal height, lacking a mesial marginal groove

question: From the occlusal aspect, the crown outline of the permanent maxillary first premolar is distinctly:
options: Hexagonal with the buccal half wider than the lingual half
Circular with no distinct line angles
explanation: Correct answer: A. Hexagonal with the buccal half wider than the lingual half

question: The developmental groove pattern on the occlusal table of the permanent maxillary second premolar is described as having:
options: A very long central groove with almost no supplemental grooves
A short, more irregular central groove with numerous supplemental grooves giving a wrinkled appearance
A Y-shaped groove pattern with a central pit
An H-shaped groove pattern intersecting an oblique ridge
A U-shaped crescent groove without supplemental fissures
explanation: Correct answer: B. A short, more irregular central groove with numerous supplemental grooves giving a wrinkled appearance

question: The lingual cusp of the permanent mandibular first premolar is morphologically unique because it is:
options: Twice as large as the buccal cusp
Functional and supports vertical masticatory load
Small, non-functional, and often resembles an elevated cingulum
Divided into two equal cusplets by a lingual groove
Separated from the buccal cusp by a deep straight central groove
explanation: Correct answer: C. Small, non-functional, and often resembles an elevated cingulum

question: In the permanent mandibular first premolar, the buccal and lingual triangular ridges typically unite to form a prominent:
options: Transverse ridge that divides the occlusal surface into two fossae
explanation: Correct answer: C. Transverse ridge that divides the occlusal surface into two fossae

question: A distinct developmental groove originating in the mesial triangular fossa and extending lingually between the mesial marginal ridge and the lingual cusp of the mandibular first premolar is the:
explanation: Correct answer: E. Mesiolingual developmental groove

question: From the mesial aspect of the permanent mandibular first premolar, the occlusal table slants characteristically:
options: Horizontally at a 90-degree angle to the root
Sharply toward the lingual at roughly a 45-degree inclination
Parallel to the labial crest of contour
explanation: Correct answer: B. Sharply toward the lingual at roughly a 45-degree inclination

question: The permanent mandibular second premolar most frequently presents with which occlusal cusp configuration?
options: Three-cusp type (one buccal, two lingual: mesiolingual and distolingual)
Five-cusp type identical to a molar
explanation: Correct answer: A. Three-cusp type (one buccal, two lingual: mesiolingual and distolingual)

question: In the three-cusp type of the permanent mandibular second premolar, the developmental grooves converge into a central pit to form a characteristic:
explanation: Correct answer: A. "Y" shaped groove pattern

question: Between the two lingual cusps of the three-cusp mandibular second premolar, the larger and higher cusp is the:
options: Both are strictly identical in size
explanation: Correct answer: B. Mesiolingual cusp

question: From the proximal aspect, the crowns of all mandibular premolars and molars show a rhomboidal geometric outline that characteristically:
options: Is completely vertical without any tilt
Tilts lingually relative to the long axis of the root
Tapers toward the cervical margin on both sides
explanation: Correct answer: C. Tilts lingually relative to the long axis of the root

question: In the permanent maxillary first premolar, the lingual cusp tip compared with the buccal cusp tip is:
options: Positioned directly in line with the buccal cusp tip
Higher and sharper than the buccal cusp
Located over the facial line angle
explanation: Correct answer: C. Displaced noticeably toward the mesial

question: The permanent mandibular second premolar of the two-cusp variety typically exhibits which occlusal groove pattern?
explanation: Correct answer: E. "U" (crescent) or "H" shaped groove pattern

question: What is the usual chronological age range for the clinical eruption of the permanent maxillary first premolar?

question: What is the usual chronological age range for the clinical eruption of the permanent mandibular first premolar?
explanation: Correct answer: B. 10 to 12 years

question: The canine fossa (mesial developmental depression) on the crown and root of the permanent maxillary first premolar makes this tooth:
options: Difficult to adapt matrix bands to during restorative procedures
A frequent site of enamel pearls
explanation: Correct answer: B. Difficult to adapt matrix bands to during restorative procedures

question: From the occlusal aspect, the crown of the three-cusp permanent mandibular second premolar has a geometric outline that is approximately:
options: Triangular with base on the buccal
explanation: Correct answer: E. Square or nearly square

question: The root of the permanent mandibular second premolar is:
options: Frequently bifurcated into mesial and distal roots
Single, longer and larger than the root of the mandibular first premolar
Deeply grooved by a mesiolingual furrow
explanation: Correct answer: C. Single, longer and larger than the root of the mandibular first premolar

question: In the permanent maxillary first premolar, the buccal triangular ridge and lingual triangular ridge are separated by a well-defined:
options: Central developmental groove with distinct mesial and distal triangular fossae
explanation: Correct answer: D. Central developmental groove with distinct mesial and distal triangular fossae

question: Deciduous maxillary canine erupt in the oral cavity around: (Past Paper)

question: Compared with the permanent maxillary canine, the cusp on the primary canine is much: (Past Paper)

question: Deciduous mandibular first molar erupt at the: (Past Paper)

question: The relation between the maxillary and mandibular primary teeth when in occlusion is such that each tooth occludes with two teeth of the opposing jaw. The exception of such contact lies in the: (Past Paper)
options: Mandibular Central Incisor and Maxillary canine
Maxillary Central Incisor and Maxillary first Molar
Maxillary Central Incisor and Maxillary Second Molar
Mandibular Central Incisor and Maxillary Second Molar
explanation: Correct answer: E. Mandibular Central Incisor and Maxillary Second Molar

question: Cingulum is the lingual lobe of an anterior tooth. It makes up the bulk of the cervical third of the lingual surface. The tooth with extended cingulum making a partial division of the concavity on the lingual surface below the incisal edge, into a mesial and distal fossa is: (Past Paper)
options: Both primary maxillary & mandibular lateral incisor
Both primary maxillary & mandibular central incisor

question: The primary mandibular lateral incisor is somewhat larger than the primary mandibular central incisor in all measurements. The only dimension in which the two teeth are practically identical is: (Past Paper)
explanation: Correct answer: B. Labio Lingual

question: The primary maxillary canine has a long, well-developed, sharp cusp, instead of an incisal edge that is relatively straight. Compared with that of the permanent maxillary canine, the primary maxillary canine is different from it in the following aspect: (Past Paper)
options: The cusp on the permanent canine is much longer and sharper
The crest of contour mesially is as far down toward the incisal portion in the primary maxillary canine as in the permanent canine
The distal slope of the cusp is longer than the mesial slope in the primary maxillary canine
In the primary maxillary canine, the contact areas are not at the same level
In the primary maxillary canine, the mesial slope of the cusp is longer than the distal slope
explanation: Correct answer: E. In the primary maxillary canine, the mesial slope of the cusp is longer than the distal slope

question: Little difference in functional form is evident between the primary mandibular canine and the maxillary canine. Which dimension shows outstanding variation in between the two deciduous canines, with the maxillary canine being much larger than the mandibular in that dimension? (Past Paper)

Mesio Distal Diameter at root trunk

question: In primary dentition, when the tooth emerges in the oral cavity, the root of the tooth is:

question: An anxious parent calls you that her 5-month-old child has still no teeth in his mouth then you should: (Past Paper)
options: Tell her that it is normal at this age
Refer her to an oral surgeon

question: All three roots of primary maxillary first molar can be seen from the given explanation best corresponds to which one of the following: (Past Paper)

question: Largest cusp of maxillary primary first molar is: (Past Paper)

question: Which pulp horn near the occlusal surface in deciduous molars makes the tooth vulnerable to exposure:

question: Which of the following are CORRECT features in the primary dentition, when generically comparing them to permanent teeth:

Flatter contours in the facial cervical third
Shorter root lengths versus their respective crown lengths

question: Approximately by which age have all four primary incisors erupted? (Past Paper)

The labial surface is very smooth with no developmental lines visible
The labial surface has pronounced developmental lines

question: What is the difference between the mesial and distal aspects of the primary mandibular central incisor? (Past Paper)

Mesial and distal aspects are nearly identical but the cervical line is less curved distally
Mesial surface has a concavity while the distal surface is convex
Mesial aspect has a blunt root while the distal aspect has a sharp root
There are no differences between the mesial and distal aspects

question: The enamel of deciduous teeth compared to permanent teeth is: (Past Paper)

Are more sharply demarcated and pronounced

question: The buccal and lingual surfaces of primary molars are: (Past Paper)

More bulbous at the occlusal level

question: How do the primary teeth differ in terms of pigmentation compared to permanent teeth? (Past Paper)

Primary teeth are usually less pigmented and appear whiter than permanent teeth
Primary teeth have the same level of pigmentation as permanent teeth
Primary teeth are more yellow than permanent teeth
Primary teeth are typically more translucent and less white than permanent teeth

question: The crowns of primary anterior teeth differ predominantly from permanent anterior teeth in that their mesiodistal diameter compared with their cervicoincisal length is:

question: In the primary maxillary central incisor, the incisal edge from the incisal aspect is characteristically:

Twisted distally on its root base

question: Which primary anterior tooth exhibits a crown where the mesiodistal crown width is definitively greater than the cervicoincisal crown length?
explanation: Correct answer: A. Primary maxillary central incisor

question: The primary maxillary lateral incisor differs from the primary maxillary central incisor because its:
options: Crown has a greater mesiodistal width than crown height
Cervicoincisal crown length is greater than its mesiodistal width, and incisal angles are more rounded
Root is shorter than that of the central incisor

question: On the primary maxillary canine, the cusp slopes are unique among all canines because the:
options: Mesial cusp ridge is shorter than the distal cusp ridge
Distal cusp ridge is straight while mesial is absent
Cusp tip is displaced strongly to the mesial
Distal cusp ridge is shorter than the mesial cusp ridge (mesial slope is longer)
Slopes are completely absent at eruption

question: The primary mandibular canine differs from the primary maxillary canine in that its:

Cusp tip is longer and sharper
Labial cervical ridge is twice as thick
explanation: Correct answer: A. Distal cusp slope is longer than its mesial cusp slope

question: In primary molars, the prominent cervical enamel ridge (tubercle of Zuckerkandl) is most prominently developed on the:
options: Distolingual surface of mandibular second molars
Mid-lingual surface of maxillary first molars
Distobuccal surface of maxillary second molars
Occlusal surface of mandibular first molars
explanation: Correct answer: B. Mesiobuccal surface of the crown

question: The roots of primary molars are markedly flared and bowed outward primarily to:
options: Anchor deeper into compact cortical bone
Provide accommodation for the developing crowns of succedaneous premolars
Increase the thickness of the interradicular alveolar crest
Prevent mesial drift of permanent first molars

question: The primary tooth that has an anatomical crown morphology entirely distinct and unlike any other primary or permanent tooth in either dental arch is the:

question: The primary maxillary second molar is an anatomical miniature replica of which permanent tooth?
options: Permanent maxillary first molar (including presence of Cusp of Carabelli)

question: The primary mandibular second molar anatomically closely mimics which permanent tooth?
options: Permanent mandibular first molar (having five functional cusps)
explanation: Correct answer: C. Permanent mandibular first molar (having five functional cusps)

question: The primary mandibular first molar has two main pulp canals located within its:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Mesial root

question: At the cervical line of primary teeth, the enamel rods in the cervical third are directed:
options: Horizontally or slightly occlusally, unlike permanent teeth
Strictly parallel to the dentinal tubules
explanation: Correct answer: B. Horizontally or slightly occlusally, unlike permanent teeth

question: The root trunk of primary molars is:
options: Very tall, placing the furcation near the middle of the root
Significantly longer than that of permanent molars
Completely absent, with roots emerging directly from the crown
Very short, causing the bifurcation or trifurcation to be situated close to the cervical line
Equal to half the total root length
explanation: Correct answer: D. Very short, causing the bifurcation or trifurcation to be situated close to the cervical line

question: The primary mandibular first molar typically exhibits how many developmental cusps?
explanation: Correct answer: C. Four cusps (mesiobuccal, distobuccal, mesiolingual, distolingual)

question: The primary maxillary first molar typically has how many roots?
explanation: Correct answer: A. Three roots (mesiobuccal, distobuccal, and lingual/palatal)

question: Which cusp of the primary mandibular first molar is the largest and longest?
explanation: Correct answer: A. Mesiolingual cusp

question: From the occlusal aspect, the primary maxillary first molar exhibits a crown outline that is roughly:

question: The occlusal table of primary molars compared to permanent molars is:

Proportionately twice as large as the cervical base
explanation: Correct answer: A. Markedly narrow buccolingually due to convergence of buccal and lingual surfaces

question: In primary teeth, the thickness of enamel and dentin compared to permanent teeth is:
options: Approximately half the thickness found in permanent teeth
explanation: Correct answer: A. Approximately half the thickness found in permanent teeth

question: The primary mandibular central incisor from the labial aspect is characterized by:
options: A distinct asymmetrical distal tilt of the incisal edge
Flat labial surface with complete bilateral symmetry and straight incisal edge

question: The size of pulp cavity usually depends upon: (Past Paper)

Age of tooth and history of trauma

question: Mark the incorrect statement regarding pulp chambers and pulp canals: (Past Paper)
options: Pulp horns are present on the floor of pulp chamber
Outline of pulp chamber follows the outline of crown
Pulp horns are very prominent in young individuals
Tooth can have more than one apical foramina
Pulp chambers and canals appear radiolucent in radiographs

question: The fourth root canal if present in a maxillary first molar is usually present in:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Mesiobuccal root

question: Which structural change in dentine poses a challenge during endodontic therapy in older patients? (Past Paper)
options: Reduction in pulp chamber size due to secondary / tertiary dentine deposition
Formation of a thicker hybrid layer
Presence of active odontoblasts in lateral canals
explanation: Correct answer: B. Reduction in pulp chamber size due to secondary / tertiary dentine deposition

question: In permanent teeth, the apical constriction (minor apical diameter) is clinically significant because it:
options: Represents the narrowest part of the root canal and the ideal histological termination for root canal instrumentation
Lies directly on the extreme anatomical apex in 100% of cases
Is lined entirely by primary acellular cementum
Is located 4 to 5 mm coronal to the cementodentinal junction
explanation: Correct answer: A. Represents the narrowest part of the root canal and the ideal histological termination for root canal instrumentation

question: The cementodentinal junction (CDJ) at the root apex:
options: Is always situated at the anatomical root apex
Represents the transition zone between pulp tissue and periodontal tissue where the canal transitions from dentin to cementum
Is a fixed, unchanging line throughout adult life
Lacks any nerve endings or blood vessels
explanation: Correct answer: B. Represents the transition zone between pulp tissue and periodontal tissue where the canal transitions from dentin to cementum

question: In cross-section through the cervical region, the pulp chamber of the permanent maxillary canine appears:
options: Triangular with base to the lingual
Ovoid, being significantly wider labiolingually than mesiodistally
Square with four distinct pulp horns
Kidney-shaped with a deep distal depression

question: When viewing the pulp chamber of a permanent mandibular second premolar of the three-cusp type, how many pulp horns are typically present?
options: Two pulp horns of equal height
Three pulp horns (one large buccal and two smaller lingual horns)
explanation: Correct answer: C. Three pulp horns (one large buccal and two smaller lingual horns)

question: The pulp chamber floor of permanent maxillary molars is characterized by developmental grooves connecting the orifices; its geometric shape is generally:
options: Triangular or trapezoidal/rhomboidal, with the palatal orifice positioned most lingually
Square with four equally spaced orifices
Linear in a straight mesiodistal orientation
C-shaped wrapping around the facial wall
explanation: Correct answer: B. Triangular or trapezoidal/rhomboidal, with the palatal orifice positioned most lingually

question: Lateral (accessory) canals in the apical third of permanent teeth are formed embryologically by:
options: Localized rupture of the dental lamina
Excessive amelogenin secretion into the follicle
Localized defect or premature fragmentation in Hertwig’s Epithelial Root Sheath (HERS) prior to dentinogenesis
Incomplete fusion of calcospherites in mantle dentin
Mineralization of the pulp core blood vessels
explanation: Correct answer: C. Localized defect or premature fragmentation in Hertwig’s Epithelial Root Sheath (HERS) prior to dentinogenesis

question: In the mesial root of the permanent mandibular first molar, the two root canals (mesiobuccal and mesiolingual) are separated by a web of dentin and characteristically:
options: Frequently exhibit intercanal communications (isthmuses) and may merge into a single apical foramen
Are strictly circular in cross section
Open on the lateral surface of the alveolar crest
Disappear by age 30 due to hypercementosis
explanation: Correct answer: B. Frequently exhibit intercanal communications (isthmuses) and may merge into a single apical foramen

question: The distal root of a permanent mandibular first molar most commonly contains:
options: One broad, ribbon-like canal or two distinct canals (distobuccal and distolingual)
Three independent canals in over 80% of teeth
A single circular canal centered in the root trunk
No pulp space due to early obliteration
explanation: Correct answer: B. One broad, ribbon-like canal or two distinct canals (distobuccal and distolingual)

question: In the permanent maxillary first premolar, when two canals are present within bifurcated roots, the pulp chamber floor is located:
options: At the extreme apical third of the root
Coronal to the middle third of the root, just apical to the cervical margin
Directly at the occlusal enamel surface
Uniformly below the alveolar bone crest
explanation: Correct answer: B. Coronal to the middle third of the root, just apical to the cervical margin

question: Accessory canals located in the furcation region of permanent molars are clinically important because they:
options: Prevent the formation of bundle bone
Provide a direct pathway for periodontal-endodontic communication and lesion spread between pulp and furcation bone
Allow continuous eruption of the tooth
Eliminate the need for endodontic sealing
explanation: Correct answer: B. Provide a direct pathway for periodontal-endodontic communication and lesion spread between pulp and furcation bone

question: The major apical foramen of a mature permanent tooth is located:
options: Rarely at the exact anatomical root tip, frequently deviating 0.5 to 1.0 mm laterally
Exclusively at the central long axis of the root tip
3 mm coronal to the cementoenamel junction
Exclusively on the mesial surface of all anterior teeth
Inside the lateral periodontal ligament space only
explanation: Correct answer: A. Rarely at the exact anatomical root tip, frequently deviating 0.5 to 1.0 mm laterally

question: Age-related reduction in the volume of the coronal pulp chamber occurs in which directional pattern?
options: Uniformly from the lateral walls only
Asymmetrically, with greatest reduction occurring from the roof and floor due to occlusal function and secondary dentin deposition
Exclusively from the root canal apex toward the crown
Strictly from the mesial wall toward the distal
Only in teeth subjected to direct trauma
explanation: Correct answer: B. Asymmetrically, with greatest reduction occurring from the roof and floor due to occlusal function and secondary dentin deposition

question: In permanent mandibular incisors, when two canals (labial and lingual) are present within a single root, they:
options: Run completely divergent into separate alveolar sockets
Are easily distinguished on standard non-angulated periapical radiographs
Often merge in the apical 1 to 3 mm to exit through a single common apical foramen
Always terminate in separate distally directed foramina
explanation: Correct answer: C. Often merge in the apical 1 to 3 mm to exit through a single common apical foramen

question: The indirect factor of tooth form that compliments its function is: (Past Paper / Wheeler's Ch 5)

question: Proximal contact relation is generally influenced by all except: (Past Paper / Wheeler's Ch 5)

question: Reducing the curve of Spee can result into which feature?

Reduce the horizontal overlap of the teeth
Increase the vertical overlap of the teeth
Reduce the vertical overlap of the teeth
Can compensate for smaller maxillary teeth

question: Regarding the curve of Spee, choose the best statement:
options: Convex in maxillae and mandible both
Convex in mandible and concave in maxillae
Concave in mandible and convex in maxillae
Exists in mandible and not in maxillae

question: Which spaces are present exclusively in the mixed dentition?

question: The centric relation position, in a patient exhibiting a slide, encompasses the following features, EXCEPT:

It describes the most stable position of condyle
It is a portion that is easily achieveable but not reproductible
It is a ligament and muscle derived portion

question: Which one of the following is considered to be accessory ligament of the masticatory apparatus:
explanation: Correct answer: A. Stylomandibular ligament

question: Which of the following is an anatomical feature of articular disk:
explanation: Correct answer: A. Thick anterior & posterior bands

question: Basic structure of the temporomandibular joint consists of:
options: Condyle, mandibular fossa, disc, articular eminence
Condyle, fossa of sphenoid bone, articular eminence
Condyle, fossa of occipital bone, articular eminence
Condyle, fossa of frontal bone, articular eminence
Condyle, fossa of ethmoid bone, articular eminence
explanation: Correct answer: A. Condyle, mandibular fossa, disc, articular eminence

question: What is the primary action of the masseter muscle? (Past Paper / Wheeler's Ch 15)
explanation: Correct answer: B. Elevating the mandible

question: Which head of the lateral pterygoid muscle is primarily involved in jaw opening movements? (Past Paper / Wheeler's Ch 15)

question: The sphenomandibular ligament is a remnant of: (Past Paper / Wheeler's Ch 15)

question: The junction at the crown and root of teeth is called:

question: Upper joint cavity in temporomandibular joint allows which type of movement:

question: Most important ligament of TMJ is:
explanation: Correct answer: B. Temporomandibular ligament

question: The physiological "col" is the depression connecting the facial and lingual interdental papillae directly apical to the contact area; in a patient with a newly restored contact, recurrent interproximal gingival inflammation develops primarily because:
options: The col consists of thick orthokeratinized epithelium that sloughs continuously
The col is lined by non-keratinized epithelium that is vulnerable to bacterial plaque stagnation when contact tight seal is absent
The col is supplied solely by bone capillaries that thrombose readily
The interdental papilla contains no elastic fibers
The col is formed exclusively by primary acellular cementum
explanation: Correct answer: B. The col is lined by non-keratinized epithelium that is vulnerable to bacterial plaque stagnation when contact tight seal is absent

question: An undercontoured facial cervical ridge on a newly placed full-coverage restoration on a mandibular first premolar will clinically cause:
options: Food debris to be driven directly into the gingival crevice, leading to gingival trauma and inflammation
Excessive muscular pressure that tips the tooth buccally
Enamel chipping along the lingual cusp tip
Spontaneous obliteration of the pulp chamber
explanation: Correct answer: B. Food debris to be driven directly into the gingival crevice, leading to gingival trauma and inflammation

question: An overcontoured restoration with excessive facial convexity in the cervical third of a permanent molar leads to periodontal pathology because it:
options: Prevents physiological self-cleansing and mechanical stimulation by deflecting food entirely away from the gingival margin, allowing plaque accumulation
Drives food forcefully into the base of the periodontal pocket
Exerts direct compressive ischemia on the alveolar bone proper
Alters the trajectory of the Curve of Wilson across the arch
Accelerates secondary dentin apposition within the pulp horns
explanation: Correct answer: A. Prevents physiological self-cleansing and mechanical stimulation by deflecting food entirely away from the gingival margin, allowing plaque accumulation

question: During routine masticatory movements, the four embrasure spaces surrounding each proximal contact area function biomechanically to:
options: Increase the absolute surface area available for bacterial adhesion
Provide escape spillways for food during crushing and reduce occlusal loading on the supporting tissues
Prevent the physiological mesial drift of permanent molars
Maintain a rigid, immovable contact during heavy lateral excursive loads
Eliminate the need for transseptal fibers between adjacent roots
explanation: Correct answer: B. Provide escape spillways for food during crushing and reduce occlusal loading on the supporting tissues

question: In permanent teeth, the curvature of the cervical line (cementoenamel junction) is universally:
options: Greater on the distal surface than on the mesial surface
Greater on the mesial surface than on the distal surface
Identical in millimeter depth on all four proximal surfaces of every tooth
Convex toward the incisal on the facial and lingual surfaces
Straight across the proximal surfaces and curved only on facial aspects
explanation: Correct answer: B. Greater on the mesial surface than on the distal surface

question: When progressing posteriorly along the dental arch from incisors to molars, the depth of proximal cervical line curvature:
options: Increases progressively from 3.5 mm to over 6 mm
Decreases progressively until it becomes almost flat on molars
Remains strictly identical on all permanent teeth
Inverts, becoming concave toward the occlusal table
Disappears entirely in all succedaneous teeth
explanation: Correct answer: B. Decreases progressively until it becomes almost flat on molars

question: On a standard bite-wing radiograph, a clinician notices that the alveolar bone crest between two mandibular molars is normally located at what distance apical to the cementoenamel junctions?
options: 1.0 to 2.0 mm apical to the CEJ
4.0 to 5.0 mm apical to the CEJ
0.2 mm apical to the marginal ridge
explanation: Correct answer: B. 1.0 to 2.0 mm apical to the CEJ

question: A radiograph of a newly erupted mandibular first permanent molar reveals a wide radiolucent funnel at the root apex surrounded by a corticated crypt. This appearance indicates:
options: Acute periapical abscess requiring emergency endodontics
Incomplete root development with an open apex and normal dental papilla
Radicular cyst formation derived from rests of Malassez
Complete pulpal necrosis due to traumatic occlusal contact
Root fracture along the developmental groove
explanation: Correct answer: B. Incomplete root development with an open apex and normal dental papilla

question: On periapical radiographs, the "cervical burnout" phenomenon frequently mistaken for interproximal root caries is caused by:
options: Localized demineralization of root dentin by acidic saliva
Lower radiopacity in the cervical region between the dense enamel cap and the alveolar bone crest
Resorption of the lamina dura by odontoclasts
Artifact from excessive lead foil exposure
explanation: Correct answer: B. Lower radiopacity in the cervical region between the dense enamel cap and the alveolar bone crest

question: In Bonwill's classic geometric description of the mandibular arch, an equilateral triangle with 4-inch (10 cm) sides is formed between the:
options: Incisal edges of the two central incisors and the mental protuberance
Center of each condyle and the mesial contact point of the mandibular central incisors
Buccal cusp tips of the two first molars and the incisal edge of the canine
Pterygoid foveae and the posterior border of the hard palate
Center of the two mandibular second premolars and the lingual frenum
explanation: Correct answer: B. Center of each condyle and the mesial contact point of the mandibular central incisors

question: The sphere of Monson combines which two anatomical curves into a single three-dimensional sphere with an 8-inch diameter (4-inch radius) centered in the glabella?
options: Curve of Spee and Curve of Wilson
Transverse palatine arch and Curve of Barker
Incisal plane and Frankfurt horizontal line
Sagittal condylar path and Bennett angle
explanation: Correct answer: A. Curve of Spee and Curve of Wilson

question: In Angle's Class I dental relationship (neutroclusion), the primary occlusal key is:
options: The mesiobuccal cusp of the maxillary first molar occludes in the mesiobuccal groove of the mandibular first molar
The distobuccal cusp of the maxillary first molar occludes in the central pit of the mandibular second molar
The maxillary canine occludes completely distal to the mandibular first premolar
The incisal edges of maxillary and mandibular incisors meet in edge-to-edge relation
The lingual cusps of mandibular molars overlap the buccal cusps of maxillary molars
explanation: Correct answer: A. The mesiobuccal cusp of the maxillary first molar occludes in the mesiobuccal groove of the mandibular first molar

question: In mutually protected occlusion (canine-protected occlusion), during a right lateral excursive movement:
options: All maxillary and mandibular posterior teeth on the right side remain in heavy group contact
The right maxillary and mandibular canines contact, completely discluding all posterior teeth on both working and non-working sides
The left non-working molars contact heavily to stabilize the TMJ
Only the incisors make contact while canines are bypassed
The inferior head of the lateral pterygoid relaxes completely on the left side
explanation: Correct answer: B. The right maxillary and mandibular canines contact, completely discluding all posterior teeth on both working and non-working sides
